answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned over time rather than just a deposit: like a willow that bends but stays rooted, an agent's history of useful work in the shared garden of tasks becomes its identity anchor. Newcomers start with a low trust pulse - limited rights that grow only through verified, peer-attested contributions - so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys no influence, because influence must be grown, not bought.
